description: Two-part query-side gate against presenting/planning non-plannable issues: layered plannability predicate (specified+open core vs core+!blocked), cam issue list --json machine mode, static spine guard banning inline stage literals, and docs mandating backlog derivation via the CLI only.

userStories.title: Extract layered plannability predicate and route all inline call sites
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need the duplicated stage+status predicate extracted into one canonical module with two layers (a specified+open universe core, and isPlannable = core + not-blocked) so that no code path reimplements plannability inline and the rank/gate universes keep their blocked-retaining semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: A new leaf module src/issues/plannable.ts exports isSpecifiedOpen(entry): boolean (entry.stage === 'specified' && entry.status === 'open') and isPlannable(entry, backlog): boolean (isSpecifiedOpen(entry) && !isBlocked(entry, backlog)); it imports only src/issues/types.ts and src/issues/graph.ts (no rank.ts/select.ts import, avoiding the select<->rank module cycle). [oracle: file-assert grep -E "export function (isSpecifiedOpen|isPlannable)" src/issues/plannable.ts shows both, and grep of its imports shows neither rank.ts nor select.ts]

src/issues/select.ts re-exports isPlannable and isSpecifiedOpen from plannable.ts, satisfying the spec's 'exported from select.ts' contract. [oracle: file-assert grep -q "plannable.ts" src/issues/select.ts and a test imports isPlannable from src/issues/select.ts]

Selection/plan-queue routes call isPlannable: selectPlannableIssue (src/issues/select.ts:67-72), selectPlannableById (src/issues/select.ts:135-138), and resolveSpecificIssue (src/commands/plan.ts:147). [oracle: bun test plus the grep oracle below]

Universe routes call isSpecifiedOpen (NOT isPlannable): rankIssues (src/issues/rank.ts:212-214) and runGraphGate universe build (src/issues/gate.ts:149-151). Blocked issues MUST remain in both universes: the rank universe retains blocked issues for topological ordering and the gate universe retains them for cycle detection. Existing rank/gate tests pass unchanged. [oracle: bun test test/issues/]

Behavior is unchanged on both layers: the selection queue (selectPlannableIssue / selectPlannableById / cam plan N validation) excludes blocked issues exactly as before, while rankIssues and runGraphGate produce identical output for a backlog containing a blocked specified+open issue (add or keep a test asserting a blocked issue is ranked and cycle-checked but never selected). [oracle: bun test]

The literal comparison === 'specified' / === "specified" appears in exactly one file under src/ outside src/vendor/: the canonical module src/issues/plannable.ts. src/vendor/ is excluded because src/vendor/_generated.ts is an auto-generated build-time embed mirroring human-facing prose (it is already excluded from typecheck by design). [oracle: grep -rElE "===\s*['\"]specified['\"]" src --include='*.ts' | grep -v '^src/vendor/' outputs only src/issues/plannable.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/issues/plannable.ts (new), src/issues/select.ts, src/issues/rank.ts, src/issues/gate.ts, src/commands/plan.ts, test/issues/*. AUDITOR FINDING 1: gate.ts:150 inline-compares the same predicate and MUST be routed through isSpecifiedOpen (it was missing from the previous plan's call-site list). AUDITOR FINDING 3: do NOT route rank.ts:213 or gate.ts:150 through isPlannable; those universes intentionally retain blocked issues (topological ranking, cycle detection). Only select.ts and plan.ts use the blocked-excluding isPlannable. Why a leaf module: select.ts imports computeWsjf from rank.ts, so rank.ts importing from select.ts would create a module cycle; plannable.ts (types.ts + graph.ts only) breaks it, and select.ts re-exports for the spec's public-surface contract. plan.ts:158 buildNotPlannableReason uses !== 'specified' for diagnostics; the guard bans only ===, leave it but consider rewriting it via the predicates for coherence (optional, do not force). list.ts:134 compares stage against a loop VARIABLE (issue.stage === stage), not the literal; it is not a predicate reimplementation and is out of scope here. Gotcha (patterns.md CAM-106 bullet): 'gate-as-code invariant' text references select.ts filtering inline; behavior stays identical so no patterns.md edit required, but append a bullet documenting the new canonical module.

userStories.title: Add cam issue list --json machine mode
userStories.description: As the orchestrator (and any machine consumer), I need `cam issue list --json` to emit a structured backlog snapshot so that backlog derivation never requires grepping scripts/cam/issues/*.json raw, where abandoned zombies (stage:specified + status:abandoned) resurrect as plannable.
acceptanceCriteria: cam issue list --json (issue_system 'none') writes to stdout a single JSON object with exactly the shape { counts: { idea, specified, planned }, plannable: [{ id, title, rank }], byStage: { idea: [...], specified: [...], planned: [...] } }; with --all, counts and byStage additionally include shipped. Output is pure JSON (no emitTitle/heading decoration) and parses with JSON.parse. [oracle: bun test asserting JSON.parse(capturedOutput) deep-equals the expected object]

counts counts only status:'open' entries per stage; status:'abandoned' entries appear NOWHERE (not in counts, not in plannable, not in byStage), including a fixture with stage:'specified' + status:'abandoned' (the CAM-99/103/130/184 zombie class); shipped appears only with --all. [oracle: bun test with an abandoned-specified fixture asserting zero occurrences of its id in the emitted JSON]

plannable membership is computed by isPlannable from src/issues/select.ts (specified + open + not blocked), and is ordered ranked-first ascending rank, then unranked, with ascending numeric id suffix as tie-break; a blocked specified+open fixture is present in byStage.specified but absent from plannable. [oracle: bun test]

The --json path reads the backlog via readBacklogFromMain (git ls-tree + cat-file --batch from the main ref), the same source as the human-readable path, never a raw working-tree read. [oracle: bun test using the recording-fake BacklogSpawnFn asserting the ls-tree/cat-file calls]

--json with issue_system 'linear'/'github' keeps the existing backend-hint behavior and exits 0 (those backends own their listing UX); the JSON contract applies to the 'none' backend. [oracle: bun test]
Parser: --json is accepted by the issue-list arg parsing (combinable with --all); `cam issue --help` / usage text documents it. [oracle: bun test + file-assert grep -q 'json' index.ts usage block]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/issues/list.ts (pure JSON-view derivation next to deriveBacklogView), src/commands/issue-list.ts (emit path + option), src/commands/issue.ts (parseIssueArgs discriminated union gains json flag on the list mode; see patterns.md CAM-190 US-003 bullet on reserved-word positional ordering), index.ts (usage text). Depends on US-001 (imports isPlannable via select.ts). Ordering nuance: the spec says plannable is 'identical to selectPlannableIssue's queue'; that means identical MEMBERSHIP predicate. Do NOT assert plannable[0] === selectPlannableIssue's champion in tests: champion selection has a WSJF unranked-vs-ranked rule (CAM-203) that can differ from rank-asc ordering. Sorting helper compareBacklogEntries in src/issues/list.ts already implements ranked-first/rank-asc/numeric-id ordering; reuse it. Use the withWriter seam + recording BacklogSpawnFn fixture pattern (patterns.md CAM-190 US-002 bullet) for deterministic tests. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/regex indexing.

userStories.title: Spine guard test banning inline === 'specified' outside the canonical module
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need a static guard in the test spine that fails when any src/ file (outside the canonical predicate module and the auto-generated vendor embed) inline-compares stage against the 'specified' literal, so that the predicate can never silently re-duplicate.
acceptanceCriteria: A new test scans every .ts file under src/, EXCLUDING src/vendor/ (auto-generated build-time embed that mirrors human-facing prose, e.g. src/vendor/_generated.ts:33 embeds the string stage === 'specified' verbatim from templates/commands/cam-plan.md; it is already excluded from typecheck by design and is out of scan scope), and fails if the regex /===\s*['\"]specified['\"]/ matches in any scanned file other than the single allowlisted src/issues/plannable.ts. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'src/vendor' test/<guard file> confirming the exclusion is explicit and documented in a comment]
The guard passes on the current tree (post US-001/US-002). [oracle: bun test]

The scanner logic is itself unit-tested: extracted as a pure function taking (filePath, content) or (fileList, readFn) so a test feeds a synthetic violating content and asserts the guard reports it, without writing a real violating file into src/. [oracle: bun test]

The guard cannot self-trip: the test file lives under test/ and the scan scope is src/ only, so the banned string inside the guard's own source is out of scope by construction (documented in a comment). [oracle: file-assert the guard file is under test/ and its scan root is src/]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: test/spine/no-inline-specified-predicate.test.ts (new; mirror existing test layout under test/). Depends on US-001 (allowlist target is src/issues/plannable.ts) and runs after US-002 so the new list code is covered. AUDITOR FINDING 2: the previous plan's single-file allowlist over ALL of src/ was unachievable because src/vendor/_generated.ts embeds the literal (and every embed-vendor regen re-injects it); the scanner MUST exclude src/vendor/ and say why in a comment. Allowlist is exactly one file: src/issues/plannable.ts (not select.ts; select.ts only re-exports and must contain no literal). Use Bun.file/readdir recursion or Bun.$ glob for enumeration (Bun-only, no node:fs preference). noUncheckedIndexedAccess: regex match groups are T | undefined.

userStories.title: Docs: mandate backlog derivation via cam issue list --json only
userStories.description: As the operator, I need the orchestrator agent instructions and the /cam-issue command doc (both dual copies) to mandate deriving the backlog exclusively via `cam issue list` / `cam issue list --json` and never by reading scripts/cam/issues/*.json raw, so that the 2026-07-08 incident (raw stage grep resurrecting 4 abandoned issues as plannable) cannot recur.
acceptanceCriteria: subagent-orchestrator.md in BOTH .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/ instructs deriving the backlog ONLY via `cam issue list` (human) / `cam issue list --json` (machine), and the current fallback instruction to read scripts/cam/issues/*.json directly filtered by stage (.claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md around line 69) is replaced by the --json instruction with an explicit prohibition on raw grep/read of scripts/cam/issues/*.json for backlog derivation. [oracle: grep -q 'issue list --json' on all four touched files, and grep of the orchestrator copies shows no instruction to read issues/*.json as a backlog-derivation path]

cam-issue.md in BOTH .claude/commands/ and templates/commands/ carries the same rule: backlog queries go through `cam issue list [--json]`, never raw issue-file reads. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'issue list --json' .claude/commands/cam-issue.md templates/commands/cam-issue.md]

Each dual-copy pair is diffed BEFORE editing and the same semantic edit is applied to each copy (the pairs are NOT byte-identical by design; do not blind-copy one over the other). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Vendor embed is regenerated (bun run embed-vendor) and the drift check passes. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]

No migration of the existing zombies (CAM-99/103/130/184): abandon-preserves-stage is intentional and they are already excluded from every output by status; no issue file under scripts/cam/issues/ is modified by this story. [oracle: git diff --name-only main... shows no scripts/cam/issues/ changes]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
